records.title: Show HN: Agents infer Lego mechanisms from sources, then animate them
records.author: antelocnova
records.storyText:
Hi there :)

Around a month ago, I released LDraw Nova, an agentic toolset for assembling LEGO CAD models by generating LDraw source code files.

For more details, here's the Show HN post:

https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49937916

From the comments, I got the impression that there was quite an interest in seeing not only AI-generated LEGO models, but also AI-animated LEGO ones.

I took a look at results from past experiments, and found it feasible to use agentic LLMs for:

- analyzing the LDraw source code for LEGO models - reverse-engineer! the mechanisms present by reading the descriptions and sequence for the parts there - and then, animate them via Blender!

This new project I'm presenting, LDraw Mecha, is the end result and proof that can be done:

- Read specially annotated LDraw LEGO models .mpd source files - Infer the model structure in terms of submodels - Select from those the ones that are mechanisms - Plan animations - Execute them in Blender

In summary, from an initial .mpd source file, get a rigged and animated version for the model as a Blender (.blend) file.

See the results here:

- Repo (v0.5.0): https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/tree/v0.5.0 - Gallery: https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/blob/v0.5.0/GALLERY.m... - Process: https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/blob/v0.5.0/PROCESS.m...

This project is very unusual, I'd really appreciate some feedback from the community.

Cheers!

records.title: Show HN: An online shop where your friends can hurry the courier
records.author: AmsterErdo
records.storyText:
I built an emulator of a flash-sale fashion outlet with no registration and fake checkout that never takes money. You can browse items that are on sale, watch in real time as they go out of stock one by one, and get notified when they are back on sale (possibly with different prices).

Every order placed on the website gets “tracking” which fails on the delivery day with one of 50 available reasons (for example, “a raccoon in the Newark depot has claimed your parcel; animal control reports that it seems happy there”). But you can also share the tracking with your friends, and they can hurry the courier; the more hurries, the more spectacularly it fails, until your parcel lands in the Svalbard seed vault, the North Pole, the International Space Station or some such place.

The complete shop contents (campaigns, prices, item availability and stock levels) are computed from the current time with a fixed seed (FNV-1a for hashing, mulberry32 as the PRNG). I wrote the mechanism first in JS and then ported to PHP (for the website) and Flutter (for the mobile app); a test ran over several thousand random time points to verify they are identical. The Flutter app uses its own generator because it can work offline - no contact with the website is necessary.

Item images are generated with OpenAI API, except models in swimsuits. OpenAI refused a lot of swimsuit image prompts, so I had to switch to Gemini for these as Gemini has no qualms about this kind of content.

Does this kind of site feel like shopping to you? Or more like a game or something to do together with friends?

If you'd be willing to check it out you can view lanterns without any signup or anything. But to launch one yourself, it requires an account (all free of course and Google and Apple OAuth supported). Only cities are shown for locations (never addresses).

Does the idea of watching your own lanterns float around the world in real-time and seeing others catch them interest you enough to come back to, or does it need more?

records.author: nkotov
records.storyText:
Hello HN, I'm Nik. I built Infinity for myself because I tend to love to rabbit-hole on various subjects.

I usually have 3-4 windows open for ChatGPT desktop + Claude + Ollama. Typically, I'd ask a question, see something interesting in the answer, and then keep expanding on it. The mental chain of thought eventually gets lost and I would start from scratch again. Second, I also wanted to compare answers across multiple models. From there, pick and use the best one and continue.

So I built Infinity for myself. Multiple windows, multiple chats. Projects all aligned in one place. But the best part is when you start highlighting any part of the response - you can branch off and fork into new chat sessions from there without losing your original chain of thought.

It's a native Mac app written in Swift. You can use all the popular cloud models that you already pay for but on top of that, you can use local models as well. You can even set out what each model's job is and assign certain models for certain jobs.

It's free, there's no account, no analytics on the actual app. Everything is stored locally. Just download, connect up, and get going.

Still extremely early but if there is interest, would love to hear what works and what doesn't!

records.title: Show HN: Retex, a Faster LaTeX Engine
records.author: skadge
records.storyText:
retex is a clean-room, CC0, reimplementation of LuaLaTeX in rust. It can either be used as a faster (x2-3) drop-in replacement for LuaLaTex (--compat mode) , or as a more modern TeX engine, with much nicer error messages, support for SVG, ODP/ODT output, native PDF/X1 and PDF/X4 for printing, auto-download of missing packages (like eg Miktex), python bindings, etc. User manual with examples: https://retex-ef747d.gitlab.io/retex-manual.pdf

retex has been entirely generated by a Large Language Model (LLM). Therefore, retex itself does not have any author. It is an automatic machine-translation of the work of D.E. Knuth and of the hundreds of volunteers who made TeX, LaTeX and LuaTeX what they are today. All credit goes to them.

records.title: Show HN: Self-Annotating Stock Charts
records.author: regnull
records.storyText:
Most stock charts work in a similar way - they give you a bunch of tools to draw lines and patterns on a chart. This is fine, and I assume that advanced traders enjoy drawing on the chart. But it's also annoying, and seems arbitrary sometimes.

So I created stock charts that annotate themselves. The process has two stages:

First, the algorithm goes through the daily candles and identifies the structure: support and resistance zones, trendlines, volume spikes, etc.

Then, an LLM models understands the relative importance of the structure components, decides which ones to include, and annotates them.

Finally, it lays out the possible future moves: base case, bull and bear cases.

It's included in Portfolio Genius, the AI investment manager I'm building, and it's available free without signup here: https://portfoliogenius.ai/features/ai-annotated-charts

records.title: Show HN: Jev vs. OpenAI Decision vs. Small Financial World Models: FinBench [video]
records.author: atul-mehra
records.storyText:
Guys - OpenAI Decisions, Jev, World Models are interesting.

We ran some tests for the C-suite to decide between OpenAI Decisions vs. their own existing models vs. training their proprietary Financial World Model. Sharing the results of our sample tests.

If you like a walkthrough with video of results - see this video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN1LIF01uHQ

We are also trying to reach OpenAI team & community to collaborate on running various tests to help the C-suite to make decisions. Which involves which business cases, they wish to map on which Decision models.

Summary: Small Financial World Model compared to OpenAI Decisions.

This test is not to build a better model. But to help C-suites make informed choices. There are various considerations viz

Latency Cost per decision On-premises or Hosted APIs Regulatory & Compliance Mapping to use cases Financial modelling or LLM-based reasoning as underlying architecture We ran tests to:

Predict credit defaults Cross-sell propensity Churn Risk Future cash flows Future state of customers & causal impacts of interventions like no-action, Payment reminders etc.

These tests are specific to banking use cases.

Why Benchmark & comparison:

Small on-prem Decision Models are needed due to latency, cost, regulatory or protecting the proprietary data for Enterprises.

This benchmarking helps C-suite executives to decide which option - their in-house models or other options are better. Vaayu FinBench also includes some specific banking-related business cases as examples.

World Model also has action-conditioning. Thus, it predicts which decision optimizes the future outcomes. Eg Risk weighted return or prevent default. Core ask from Banks

Small Financial World Model is trained on-premesis on proprietary data for enterprises.

Scope - This is only for demonstration purposes to give a glimpse of how to compare various options. The dataset & model size is way too small yet. On a larger proprietary dataset, the results need to be benchmarked.

Results: Latency - A co-located Small Financial World Model way improves latency. Major part may be coming due to network latency. So this is one area where we would like to discuss alternatives with OpenAI team & community. Is there a smaller on-premesis version for Decision Model avaialble for co-location.

Credit Defaults - Our Small Financial World model worked worse than Decision API.

Cash Churn & Cross Sell propensity - Our Small Financial World model improved marginally. It’s obvious that since Decision API hasnt seen the propreitary data. The marginal improvement shows model is learning..but our model is very very small (Few 100 thousand parameters) trained on small dataset.. But test demonstrates - architecture is capable of learning better.

Action conditions outcomes - This is available in World Model …but we aren’t aware of this in Decision API yet.

Financial Modelling - Model is trained finance native can handle temporal & causal scenarios

If you like a walkthrough - see this video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN1LIF01uHQ

Disclaimer: This is quick tests results & has some know issues. This is only for demonstration purpose. We have included OpenAI Decisions for now...Including Jev in next releases. At the moment talking to C-suite & Banks for what they wish.

We find Decision API & World Models interesting developments especially in finance & enterprises space. Looking forward to collaborate with OpenAI team & community how to enable C-suite to make choices…which are underway right now at enterprises.

records.title: Show HN: Solous, a journaling app like a social media for emotions inside of you
records.author: solous
records.storyText:
Solous is a private journaling app. This app is inspired by movies like inside out or Yumi's Cells where we all have emotions inside us. When we write it is one of our emotions writing it. We want to talk to ourselves between these debating ideas and emotions. We are solo but also there are persons inside us. That's where the name is from solo-us. In Solous, you can reply to your own message anytime. It supports normal stuff like tag and search. I try to make it as secure as possible with e2ee as an option.

I am the sole builder of the app. I built this app mostly for myself in my free time with Claude. Yes I vibed 100% but I am familiar with aws and python, I am a decent programmer. It is true that these days, everyone can do that. But it still takes time and effort to make it run smoothly and polish features and make it easy to use. I don't believe the future of software is everyone vibe their own stuff. The most efficient way is still to use several good apps. I think there may be more diversity instead of everyone use app store or play store.

Because it is made for myself, it has no reminder emails, sometimes, I even don't journal for days, but I feel good when I write one. I think it is good to record what happened in life. Especially when I feel bad.

And it is private, it has two factor login, security keys such as face id or whatever you use to unlock your phone, and it has optional end to end encryption. At first I want to make it default, but then I realized it takes some time to setup and maybe it will reduce conversion. so I leave it for whoever care about privacy.

The app is free for now. For free tier, there is 1GB limit on uploads and how many journaling you can do (if you write on your own not using ai, you will be ok with free tier). Later I will charge money if you need more space and maybe if you want to give me more money, you can become member and maybe I will open some private features for members or provide more customization options. That's the idea. I will be around today, please try and let me know. Thank you!

records.storyText:
Hi HN, I've built Rui (cotton in hindi), an agent runtime built for memory efficiency.

The main design choice is that sessions share a host rather than each being a process. Agents are state in DB and the host handles the active work through a share event loop.

LLMs are getting better at coordination and teams (swarms) of agents are coming. Memory is getting expensive and my machine is always using swap. We cannot be wasting hundreds of MBs of RAM for an orchestrator (AKA the harness) of LLMs and tools.

More information on the architecture and measurement methodology is at https://divyanshgolyan.com/posts/hundred-agents/

I'd love feedback about this design boxing me into a corner and any large tradeoffs I'm not seeing!

records.title: Show HN: Fermi Poker, a combination of poker betting mechanics with estimation
records.author: danielfetz
records.storyText:
Throughout this year I've been working on a game called Fermi Poker and have now published a guide on how to play and host a tournament. This guide includes a question set, a rule sheet to print out, and everything else you need to know. If you don't want to print out anything, you can also use fermi.org/play to see the questions on your device.

Fermi Poker combines the betting mechanics of poker with Fermi estimation questions like "How many new smartphones were sold worldwide in 2024?" or "How many chickens were slaughtered for meat worldwide in 2024?"

Once you've submitted a range estimate, there are four betting rounds, with two hints and the answer revealed between them.

The aspiration was to create a game that teaches important rationality concepts (Fermi estimation, Bayesian updating, cognitive empathy, world-modeling, emotional regulation, etc.)

If you want to host a tournament at your school or university, please consider reaching out as I can provide some funding to cover the cost of poker chips and small prizes.

records.title: Show HN: AJX – Find out where AI agents get stuck using your product
records.author: royosherove
records.storyText:
Hi HN. I made AJX (Agent Journey Experience). It is a CLI and skill bundle that you run to test what your product feels like to use from the point of view of an agent, and you get back a list of "asks" that would improve your product from an agentic usability perspective: so that agents spend less time, tokens and retries to accomplish tasks with it.

How? It works by having an outer loop (AJX harness skill + CLI) that controls an "inner loop": the agent that actually tries out your product. The outer loop investigates the inner loop once it finishes.

To try it, copy the prompt from the main page into your favorite agent and it will install the skill and CLI and you can then trigger /ajx skill, give it a prompt and some simple configuration as text, and it helps you with the rest. The outer loop starts loading the configured harness of your choice (claude, codex, kiro-cli etc..) in an environment and configuration of your choice (docker, VM, local, with or without specific skills, specific model, amount of runs, and more), and provides the harness (inner loop) with your input prompt and links, and "definition of done" - what does it mean to succeed with this product? For example with vercel cli you could say "build and deploy a simple hello world with vercel CLI [link]" as the prompt for the AJX test.

Once the inner loop harness runs its course, the outer harness loop examines the run, logs and details, and outputs and extract the needed information from that run: retries, tokens, mistakes, assumptions and more, and created a very detailed report, as well as a list of asks that if applied to the product, would improve the agentic journey given the same prompt in the future.

I call this "Agent Journey eXperience" it's the agentic equivalent of "User Experience" - if we were to document the journey an agent does when trying your product for the first time in a specific scenario.

- Where does it go astray and makes mistakes? - How many retries does it take to succeed with the task? - How much time? - How many tokens?

List of ASKS as an output: What features/fixes would the agent want the product to have to save it from making these mistakes or costing extra time and token in the future? here are some examples: - CLI missing a --JSON, which cost lots of parsing of unneeded code - CLI missing commands like doctor, help aliases - DOCS disagree with behavior of the product - Skills pull the agent in the wrong direction - lack of feedback while product is executing - Human friendly CLIs outputs break the agent loop - and much more.

Why? I'm a startups solutions architect @ AWS, and previously wrote the art of unit testing and did lots of work on code quality, engineering practiced and continuous delivery) I built AJX (ajx.dev) when I was tasked with giving feedback on an internal upcoming AWS product that is meant to be used by agents. The team wanted feedback from potential users, and I figured that agents are the new potential users.

I figured that if I was a product owner, I'd love to know what it feels like to work with my product (CLI, SDK, Website, Docs etc), and that the harder the agents work to use my product, the less people would point their agent at it, or the less the agent would tend to recommend it. Also I think it's useful to have "brag points" that your product is "agent-friendly".

I even tested AJX with AJX and it found great of issues with the CLI (for example ajx status was returning the wrong status sometimes, ajx init --task behaved differently than expected, and other cool stuff like that.

I envision this being used as part of a CI/CD cycle with a loop until AJX returns "all green" and no ASKS.

AJX is still very new - so probably lots of rough edges but in an agent first world, I think it's a step in the right direction: see the world from an agent's POV.

records.title: Show HN: Realtime sync engine without any new infra
records.author: tanishqkanc
records.storyText:
Tandem is an open-source sync engine and client-side database that plugs into your existing infrastructure. Add the Tandem library to sync data in real time across your clients and server, without deploying any new services.

I started work on Tandem 6 years ago as a side project. I was frustrated by the sync engine landscape at the time, thinking I could build a better DX and require less lock-in. Even now, sync engine companies and “full-stack databases” need you to migrate to their database or provision a separate service with auth, networking, etc. This makes them annoying to maintain and also harder to adopt incrementally.

Tandem is designed to just be embedded into your existing frontend and backend code. You define a schema, set up a database adapter (any SQL-like database is supported), add the new sync endpoint to your existing API, and then you're good to go.

Tandem uses DST (Deterministic Simulation Testing) on every PR and nightly to ensure correctness. Our DST system Gatekeeper lets us model not only storage and network failures, but also race conditions, by gating each call between client/server/other services independently.

Tandem currently supports any React-based frontend, any serverful backend (like Cloudflare Durable Objects), and any SQL-like database. New adapters are easy to build, and PRs and issues are appreciated!

Open-source and MIT licensed: https://github.com/tanishqkancharla/tandem
